citation: Abe, Y., Thomas, V., Sinicrope, C., & Gee, K. A. (2012). Effects of the Pacific CHILD Professional Development Program (Final Report, NCEE 2013-4002). Washington, DC: National Center for Education Evaluation and Regional Assistance, Institute of Education Sciences, U.S. Department of Education.
design: Cluster RCT; assignment = School; 51 schools randomized (26 treatment / 25 control), impact analysis sample = 45 schools (23 treatment / 22 control); subject = reading (literacy); grade 5 students (TPD targeted grade 4-5 ELA teachers); three entities (American Samoa, CNMI, Hawai'i). Two-level HLM (students/teachers within schools), pretest/covariate-adjusted.
problems: No single pooled ICC is reported; the paper reports entity-specific unconditional ICCs (American Samoa .04, CNMI .06, Hawai'i .07) and conditional ICCs (Am. Samoa .04, CNMI .04, Hawai'i .01). The model already accounts for clustering (cluster_adjusted=true), so a central design-effect correction is not needed; icc left null to avoid misrepresenting a pooled value. Hawai'i used TerraNova converted to SAT-10-equivalent scores (appendix E); Am. Samoa and CNMI used the SAT-10 directly. The reported effect size (0.244) is the paper's standardized impact (HLM impact estimate divided by control-group SD); g recomputed from impact estimate (5.3) and its SE (2.19) gives the same value with J~1 for N=3,052.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Pacific CHILD TPD vs business-as-usual control (single TPD arm)
effect_sizes.test_name: Stanford Achievement Test 10th ed. (SAT-10) Reading Comprehension scale score (Hawai'i: TerraNova converted to SAT-10-equivalent)
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (spring of Year 2, end of 2-year intervention)
effect_sizes.g_method: Paper-reported standardized impact d = impact/SD_control = 5.3/21.721 = 0.244 (control-group SD standardizer), from two-level HLM, pretest/covariate-adjusted. g = J*d with J = 1-3/(4*df-1), df = N-2 = 3050, J = 0.99975. SE(d) = SE(impact)/SD_control = 2.19/21.721 = 0.1008; g_se = J*SE(d) = 0.1008; g_var = g_se^2 = 0.01016. Cross-check t = impact/SE = 2.42, matching reported p = .017.
effect_sizes.page_ref: p. xv-xvii (Exec. Summary); Table B.5 'Estimate of overall impact: weighted mean of three entity estimates (benchmark model)', p. B11 (PDF p.117); sample sizes p. xiv-xv (PDF p.15) and Figure 2.2 (PDF p.44); school counts p.34-36 (PDF p.35-36)
effect_sizes.notes: Headline confirmatory full-sample student outcome. Overall impact = weighted mean of three entity-specific HLM estimates. Entity subsamples (NOT extracted as separate full-sample rows; they are subgroups): American Samoa ES = -0.146 (n=185, p=.629), CNMI ES = 0.392 (n=692, p=.027), Hawai'i ES = 0.133 (n=2,175, p=.050). A 'combined sample' pooled estimate (entity fixed effects) gave ES = 0.068 (n=3,052, p=.247, NS) and is reported by the authors as method-sensitive; the authors adopt the weighted-mean estimate (0.244) as the primary result. A priori MDES for student outcomes was 0.16. Comparison/control = business-as-usual.
